data.sourceWord: MCQ: Which one of the following is a means of salvation in Christianity?

examples.en-GB: AQA MCQ (1 mark) — Answer: Grace | Distractors: Ascension; Sin; Trinity

data.targetWord: Christians believe heaven is where God dwells, a place of perfect goodness, peace and joy with no pain or suffering, granted to those whose sins are forgiven.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.2 (2 marks) — Give two Christian beliefs about heaven

data.targetWord: Heaven offers eternal life and reunion with family and friends in a spiritual state, often pictured as being in God's presence with the angels.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.2 (2 marks) — Give two Christian beliefs about heaven

data.targetWord: Belief in one God leads Christians to direct all worship to him alone, building a personal relationship through prayer and pilgrimage and giving him their full faith.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.3 (4 marks) — influence of the Oneness of God

data.sourceWord: Oneness of God — Trinity and mission
data.targetWord: Monotheism strengthens belief in the Trinity as three aspects of one God, and may motivate Christians to do mission and evangelism so others come to know the one God.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.3 (4 marks) — influence of the Oneness of God

data.targetWord: Jesus' crucifixion atoned for the original sin of Adam and Eve, removing the barrier between humanity and God and offering forgiveness and eternal life to those who repent.

examples.en-GB: 'For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.' (Romans 6:23)

data.targetWord: By suffering on the cross Jesus enables Christians to accept suffering in their own lives, knowing he understood human pain and that death is not the end.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.4 (5 marks) — importance of the Crucifixion

data.targetWord: 'He is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.' (1 John 2:2) — showing the universal scope of Christ's saving death.

data.sourceWord: FOR: God's love shown in Creation
data.targetWord: God created the world and all living things out of love and wants the best for his creation, which gives strong grounds for believing he is always loving.

data.sourceWord: FOR: God's love shown in the Incarnation
data.targetWord: God's most loving act was sending his Son to die for humanity: 'God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son.' (John 3:16) — the supreme demonstration of love.

data.sourceWord: FOR: God's love extends to all through forgiveness
data.targetWord: God's perfect love extends to all who ask for forgiveness; no one is excluded, and Christians are commanded to love even their enemies as God loves all.
The existence of suffering and evil is hard to reconcile with an all-loving God; if God were always loving he would prevent unnecessary suffering, yet it continues.
In the Old Testament God does not always appear loving — the drowning of the Egyptian army and the destruction of Jericho suggest a wrathful, judgemental God.
Applying the human idea of 'always loving' to an infinite God may be misleading; what seems unloving to us may serve a divine purpose we cannot understand.

data.prompt: Build a sentence: what did Jesus' crucifixion atone for?
data.answer: The crucifixion atoned for the sins of all humanity.

data.prompt: Build a sentence: what do Christians believe about heaven?
data.answer: Heaven is a place of peace and joy in the presence of God.

data.prompt: Build a sentence: what does belief in one God mean for worship?
data.answer: Christians worship only one God with their full faith.

data.title: Christian Beliefs about Salvation
data.sourcePassage: Salvation is central to Christian belief. Christians teach that human beings are separated from God by sin, beginning with the original sin of Adam and Eve. Through the crucifixion of Jesus, this barrier is removed: Jesus' death is understood as an atoning sacrifice that pays the debt of sin for all humanity. Salvation is offered as a free gift of God's grace, not earned by good works alone, and is received through faith and repentance. Christians believe that those who accept Jesus' sacrifice can be reconciled with God and receive eternal life in heaven. The resurrection of Jesus three days after the crucifixion confirms, for believers, that death is not the end and that God's love is more powerful than sin and death.
